pathway.title: Alkermes plc. — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Alkermes borrowed its full USD 1,525.0 million of term loans to buy Avadel, moving from no debt at December 31, 2025 to USD 1,497.7 million of senior secured debt at September 30, 2026. The debt is two bank term loans with no bonds. Scheduled principal is USD 6.625 million for the rest of 2026, USD 26.500 million in 2027, USD 40.563 million in 2028 and USD 45.250 million in each of 2029 and 2030, which leaves 89.1% of principal due in 2031 (new arithmetic, see Calculations) [financial base: debt and capital structure]. Liquidity of USD 787.6 million of cash and investments, with no revolver found, is what the creditor can rely on, and it comfortably covers amortization.

Leverage is the central judgement. On LTM Adjusted EBITDA of USD 440.2 million, total debt is 3.40x and net debt 1.61x, but LTM reported EBITDA is only USD 146.2 million, which gives 10.25x and 4.86x. The difference is acquisition costs, inventory step-up, share-based compensation and a contingent consideration charge, and the FY2025 part of LTM Adjusted EBITDA is derived by the analyst. Expense-basis cover is 5.08x on Adjusted EBITDA, with cash interest unreported [financial base: leverage and coverage].

Business risk is concentrated. VIVITROL was 31.7% of FY2025 revenue and generic entry is expected in 2027, while ARISTADA patents run to 2039 and LYBALVI patents to 2041, with LYBALVI facing paragraph IV challenges, and the legacy products rely on three wholesalers. LUMRYZ supplied 16.5% of nine-month 2026 revenue through four specialty pharmacies, bears a 3.85% royalty to Jazz and faces a generic challenge [business context: operating model and credit translations]. Cash from operations of USD 72.9 million for nine months 2026, against USD 350.7 million a year earlier, shows how heavily the first year of integration weighed on cash, while LTM free cash flow of USD 227.4 million shows the recovery to date [financial base: cash flow quality].

Documented behaviour is not extractive: no dividend has been paid and buybacks of USD 27.7 million occurred only in Q1 2026, but ownership, board and covenant capacity are not supplied, so legal capacity for distributions cannot be tested [business context: ownership, governance and capital allocation]. This corrects the business context handoff, which said buybacks stopped after the term loans were drawn: the sources show only that none occurred in Q2 or Q3 2026 and do not date the Q1 purchases against the February 12, 2026 closing.

runs.text: Strengths. (1) Liquidity and maturity profile: USD 787.6 million of cash and investments against light amortization and a 2031-weighted maturity wall, which gives time to absorb the 2027 VIVITROL change (Documentary Fact; financial base). (2) Cash generation: LTM free cash flow of USD 227.4 million with low capital spending, equal to 15.2% of debt (Documentary Fact for the inputs; the ratio is Analyst Interpretation). (3) Portfolio breadth beyond one product: four proprietary products plus royalties, with ARISTADA patents to 2039, LYBALVI to 2041 and LUMRYZ orphan exclusivity to 2030 for adults (Documentary Fact; business context). (4) Interest rate protection on USD 750.0 million of notional through collars entered in October 2026, though covenant effects are unknown (Documentary Fact). (5) Documented financial behaviour has been conservative: debt prepaid in 2024, no dividends, no buybacks in Q2 or Q3 2026 (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation on what it implies).

Weaknesses. (1) Dependence on add-backs: 3.40x on Adjusted EBITDA against 10.25x on reported EBITDA, with a derived FY2025 base and share-based compensation add-backs that do not tie to the statements (Documentary Fact; the dependence is Analyst Interpretation). (2) Product concentration and generic risk: VIVITROL at 31.7% of FY2025 revenue with generic entry expected in 2027, and product-level margins Not supplied, so the cash flow effect cannot be sized (Documentary Fact; Insufficient Information for the effect). (3) Secured structure without visible covenants: all debt is secured on substantially all assets, but levels, definitions and the margin grid are Not supplied, and Term Loan B is outside the maintenance tests (Insufficient Information). (4) Floating-rate exposure: Term SOFR plus 1.75% to 2.25% on Term Loan A and 2.25% on Term Loan B, half of principal hedged by collars (Documentary Fact; the share is arithmetic). (5) Acquisition accounting and contingent liability: a preliminary purchase price allocation, intangibles and goodwill that make up most of the consideration, and a possible payment of USD 165.7 million carried at USD 136.9 million (Documentary Fact; the impairment exposure is Analyst Interpretation). (6) Channel and counterparty concentration: three wholesalers for legacy products and four specialty pharmacies for LUMRYZ (Documentary Fact). (7) Thin interim cash conversion: nine-month 2026 cash from operations of USD 72.9 million (Documentary Fact).

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The Avadel Acquisition is the transaction for this run. In October 2025 the company and Avadel "entered into a definitive transaction agreement, subsequently amended in November 2025" (10-K_2025-12-31_alks-20251231.htm.jsonl page:10). The consideration is $21.00 per Avadel share in cash at closing plus a non-transferable contingent value right of $1.50 per share payable on a specified milestone (page:10). The acquisition closed on February 12, 2026 (10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl page:15). Preliminary purchase consideration was 2,306.9 US$m, being 2,064.3 US$m for Avadel shares, 134.9 US$m cash settlement of equity awards and 107.7 US$m fair value of the CVR, so cash paid at closing was 2,199.2 US$m (page:16). The potential CVR payment totals $165.7 million (page:53), and management expects the milestone to be determined by the end of 2027 (page:53); the probability of success was raised from 75% to 90% after positive phase 3 results for LUMRYZ in idiopathic hypersomnia (page:24). The type is a strategic acquisition by a listed strategic buyer; there is no sponsor.

Financing and liquidity effect (CP-1 handoff figures). Before closing the company arranged a senior secured bridge facility of up to approximately $1.5 billion in November 2025 and placed approximately $731.2 million of its cash in escrow (10-K page:193). At closing it entered the credit agreement and borrowed the full $1.525 billion available under two term loans, which replaced the bridge. After the August 12, 2026 amendment the facilities carried 1,497.7 US$m (carrying) at September 30, 2026, Term Loan A due February 12, 2031 and Term Loan B due August 12, 2031, with margins of 1.75% to 2.25% and 2.25% over Term SOFR. No bond or note issuance appears in the debt note; the new debt is bank term debt only. Liquidity at September 30, 2026 was cash and investments of 787.6 US$m with no revolving facility found in the sources. The deal moved leverage from nil at December 31, 2025 to 3.40 times LTM Adjusted EBITDA (management measure with a derived FY2025 component), per the CP-1 handoff.

Use of proceeds and status. The term loan proceeds and the escrowed cash funded the cash consideration; the cash consideration of 2,199.2 US$m less net debt proceeds of 1,511.6 US$m leaves 687.7 US$m from cash, below the escrow, and the sources do not state what the remaining escrow was used for (this is arithmetic, not a sources and uses table). The purchase price allocation is preliminary and may be adjusted for up to one year from closing (page:16). Goodwill of 509.5 US$m and acquired intangible assets of 1,794.9 US$m were recognised at closing, so identifiable intangibles are most of the consideration, and if LUMRYZ underperforms the carrying values are exposed to impairment (Analyst Interpretation; no impairment is reported). The company states it cannot present Avadel's separate net income because the businesses "do not operate as discrete entities within the Company" after integration (page:19).

Executed documents are listed as exhibits but not supplied: the Transaction Agreement and its amendment, the Credit Agreement and Amendment No. 1 (10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl page:58; 10-Q_2026-03-31_alks-20260331.htm.jsonl page:50). Terms such as the CVR milestone definition, covenant levels and guarantor names are therefore Not supplied. Subsequent to the balance sheet date and before the cutoff, in October 2026 the company entered into two interest rate collars with a total notional of 750.0 US$m (CP-1 handoff; 10-Q page:30).

LTM revenue is 1,753.6 US$m against 1,475.9 US$m in FY2025, mostly from the addition of LUMRYZ. GAAP profit is near zero over the LTM because of inventory step-up amortization, acquisition costs, intangible amortization, a contingent consideration fair value charge and 86.6 US$m of interest expense, and the management measures are the main bridge to leverage. On the management Adjusted EBITDA basis, total debt is 3.40 times LTM and net debt 1.61 times; on the company-definition reported EBITDA the same ratios are 10.25 and 4.86 times. The covenant package, the margin grid and any revolver are not readable from the pack, so headroom, undrawn liquidity and cash coverage are Not supplied. Debt service is modest through 2030 (scheduled amortization of 6.6 to 45.3 US$m a year) with nearly all principal due in 2031, which places the refinancing test in 2031.

Nine months 2026 shows an operating income of 6.1 US$m and a net loss of 49.7 US$m. Scheduled principal is 1,511.75 US$m, and the company states "At September 30, 2026, our borrowings consisted of $1.511 billion outstanding under the Facilities." (page:55). Unamortized discount and fees are "$3.6 million and $10.4 million, respectively" (page:30). The facilities were drawn in full at closing at 1,525.0 US$m: "the Company borrowed the full $1.525 billion available under the Facilities" (10-K_2025-12-31_alks-20251231.htm.jsonl page:193). Pricing after the amendment is Term SOFR plus 1.75% to 2.25% on Term Loan A, set by a Secured Net Leverage Ratio grid that is not supplied, and Term SOFR plus 2.25% on Term Loan B; the amendment cut the spread by 0.75% on Term Loan A and 0.50% on Term Loan B (page:28). The original margin was 2.75% on both (10-Q_2026-03-31_alks-20260331.htm.jsonl page:23). Three-month SOFR was 4.07% at September 30, 2026, and the company estimates that a 10% rise in the rate would raise interest from October 1 to December 31, 2026 by $1.6 million (10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl page:55).

The amendment was accounted for lender by lender, with three exiting Term Loan B lenders treated as extinguished and one new lender as new issuance (page:29), with a 0.5 US$m write-off of deferred costs and 2.6 US$m of arranger fees in Q3 interest expense.

No revolving facility, undrawn committed facility or letter of credit line is described in any pinned source, so undrawn committed facilities are Not supplied and available liquidity is cash and investments only; this is the finding of the searched text and not proof that none exists. The only letters of credit mentioned are collateralised by held-to-maturity investments tied to leases (10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl page:50). fields.value: Cash flow from operations was 72.9 US$m for nine months 2026 against 350.7 US$m for nine months 2025 (10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl page:7). The 2026 figure is after a net loss of 49.7 US$m, add-backs of 94.2 US$m share-based compensation, 76.9 US$m depreciation and amortization, 72.4 US$m inventory step-up amortization and 27.0 US$m contingent consideration fair value, and a working capital outflow of 156.8 US$m (page:51), including a 116.4 US$m outflow in accounts payable and accrued expenses (page:7). Capital expenditure was low at 15.6 US$m. Cash taxes paid were 34.9 US$m against 3.1 US$m (page:8). Free cash flow, defined here as cash from operations less additions of property, plant and equipment, was 57.3 US$m for nine months 2026 and 227.4 US$m over the LTM, against 480.3 US$m in FY2025. Q3 2026 alone generated 93.5 US$m of operating cash flow (derived by subtraction), which suggests recovery after the heavy first half, but one quarter is not a trend. Share-based compensation is large relative to Adjusted EBITDA: the release adds back 112.6 US$m of it in nine months 2026 against Adjusted EBITDA of 339.5 US$m. It is a non-cash but recurring cost, and the sources do not say whether it is settled in cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage. On total debt of 1,497.7 US$m (carrying) and LTM Adjusted EBITDA of 440.2 US$m (derived, see below), total debt to EBITDA is 3.40 times; net debt of 710.2 US$m gives 1.61 times. On principal of 1,511.75 US$m the ratios are 3.43 and 1.65 times. On LTM reported EBITDA of 146.2 US$m the ratios are 10.25 and 4.86 times. The gap between the bases is explained by add-backs of acquisition-related costs, share-based compensation and the inventory step-up that flows through cost of goods sold; the step-up is non-cash and, as an analyst inference, should roll off as the acquired inventory is sold, whereas share-based compensation is a recurring cost. At December 31, 2025 there was no debt; net debt was negative 588.4 US$m (cash 388.6 plus investments 199.8), and 731.2 US$m of restricted cash is excluded from that figure.

fields.value: Coverage. Cash paid for interest is not presented for any 2026 period (the supplemental cash flow disclosure shows taxes only), and the 10-K shows cash paid for interest of nil in FY2025, so EBITDA to cash interest is Not supplied. Interest expense includes non-cash and one-off items: 7.4 US$m of bridge facility financing costs in the nine months, 2.6 US$m of arranger fees and 0.5 US$m of deferred cost write-off in Q3, and amortization of discount and fees of 0.6 US$m in Q3. An analyst estimate that removes the Q3 items gives about 23.9 US$m for the quarter, an annualised 95.4 US$m, but this is an estimate, not a reported figure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Alkermes plc is an Irish-incorporated, Nasdaq-listed neuroscience company with U.S. commercial operations. Before 2026 its earnings came from three proprietary U.S. products (VIVITROL, ARISTADA and ARISTADA INITIO, LYBALVI) and from royalty and manufacturing revenue on long-acting antipsychotics sold by Janssen and on VUMERITY sold by Biogen. The Avadel Pharmaceuticals plc acquisition, completed on February 12, 2026, added LUMRYZ and its commercial organisation, was financed by senior secured term loans and balance sheet cash, and created a contingent value right that can add a further cash payment. The transaction is the dominant credit event in the pack: it moved the company from no debt at December 31, 2025 to senior secured term loans, it brought acquired intangibles and goodwill that make up most of the purchase price, and it changed the revenue mix toward a product distributed through a closed pharmacy network. The creditor-relevant business risks are concentration in a few products and three wholesalers, expected VIVITROL generic entry in 2027, patent challenges against LYBALVI and LUMRYZ, government rebate exposure, and reliance on the pipeline (alixorexton, ALKS 7290) for growth that the debt service does not depend on today. Mitigants documented in the pack are that ARISTADA patents run to 2039 and LYBALVI patents to 2041, that LUMRYZ has orphan drug exclusivity through May 1, 2030 for adults, that no dividends have been paid, and that the company reports cash and investments of 787.6 US$m at September 30, 2026 (from the CP-1 handoff). Ownership and board composition are Not supplied, so sponsor and control analysis is limited to documented corporate actions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The Avadel Acquisition is the transaction for this run. In October 2025 the company and Avadel "entered into a definitive transaction agreement, subsequently amended in November 2025" (10-K_2025-12-31_alks-20251231.htm.jsonl page:10). The consideration is $21.00 per Avadel share in cash at closing plus a non-transferable contingent value right of $1.50 per share payable on a specified milestone (page:10). The acquisition closed on February 12, 2026 (10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl page:15). Preliminary purchase consideration was 2,306.9 US$m, being 2,064.3 US$m for Avadel shares, 134.9 US$m cash settlement of equity awards and 107.7 US$m fair value of the CVR, so cash paid at closing was 2,199.2 US$m (page:16). The potential CVR payment totals $165.7 million (page:53), and management expects the milestone to be determined by the end of 2027 (page:53); the probability of success was raised from 75% to 90% after positive phase 3 results for LUMRYZ in idiopathic hypersomnia (page:24). The type is a strategic acquisition by a listed strategic buyer; there is no sponsor.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financing and liquidity effect (CP-1 handoff figures). Before closing the company arranged a senior secured bridge facility of up to approximately $1.5 billion in November 2025 and placed approximately $731.2 million of its cash in escrow (10-K page:193). At closing it entered the credit agreement and borrowed the full $1.525 billion available under two term loans, which replaced the bridge. After the August 12, 2026 amendment the facilities carried 1,497.7 US$m (carrying) at September 30, 2026, Term Loan A due February 12, 2031 and Term Loan B due August 12, 2031, with margins of 1.75% to 2.25% and 2.25% over Term SOFR. No bond or note issuance appears in the debt note; the new debt is bank term debt only. Liquidity at September 30, 2026 was cash and investments of 787.6 US$m with no revolving facility found in the sources. The deal moved leverage from nil at December 31, 2025 to 3.40 times LTM Adjusted EBITDA (management measure with a derived FY2025 component), per the CP-1 handoff.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Use of proceeds and status. The term loan proceeds and the escrowed cash funded the cash consideration; the cash consideration of 2,199.2 US$m less net debt proceeds of 1,511.6 US$m leaves 687.7 US$m from cash, below the escrow, and the sources do not state what the remaining escrow was used for (this is arithmetic, not a sources and uses table). The purchase price allocation is preliminary and may be adjusted for up to one year from closing (page:16). Goodwill of 509.5 US$m and acquired intangible assets of 1,794.9 US$m were recognised at closing, so identifiable intangibles are most of the consideration, and if LUMRYZ underperforms the carrying values are exposed to impairment (Analyst Interpretation; no impairment is reported). The company states it cannot present Avadel's separate net income because the businesses "do not operate as discrete entities within the Company" after integration (page:19).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Alkermes plc is a moderately leveraged specialty drug company whose secured term loans look serviceable from current cash flow, but whose coverage depends on managing expected VIVITROL generic entry in 2027 and on integrating LUMRYZ. The strongest support is liquidity: USD 787.6 million of cash and investments against USD 26.5 million of principal due in 2027 and only USD 164.2 million due before 2031. The weakest point is that total debt of USD 1,497.7 million is 3.40x LTM Adjusted EBITDA but 10.25x reported EBITDA, so leverage rests on management add-backs, and covenant levels cannot be read. The outcome will be decided by whether legacy cash flow is replaced as VIVITROL erodes, and by the covenant terms not yet supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Alkermes borrowed its full USD 1,525.0 million of term loans to buy Avadel, moving from no debt at December 31, 2025 to USD 1,497.7 million of senior secured debt at September 30, 2026. The debt is two bank term loans with no bonds. Scheduled principal is USD 6.625 million for the rest of 2026, USD 26.500 million in 2027, USD 40.563 million in 2028 and USD 45.250 million in each of 2029 and 2030, which leaves 89.1% of principal due in 2031 (new arithmetic, see Calculations) [financial base: debt and capital structure]. Liquidity of USD 787.6 million of cash and investments, with no revolver found, is what the creditor can rely on, and it comfortably covers amortization.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is the central judgement. On LTM Adjusted EBITDA of USD 440.2 million, total debt is 3.40x and net debt 1.61x, but LTM reported EBITDA is only USD 146.2 million, which gives 10.25x and 4.86x. The difference is acquisition costs, inventory step-up, share-based compensation and a contingent consideration charge, and the FY2025 part of LTM Adjusted EBITDA is derived by the analyst. Expense-basis cover is 5.08x on Adjusted EBITDA, with cash interest unreported [financial base: leverage and coverage].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business risk is concentrated. VIVITROL was 31.7% of FY2025 revenue and generic entry is expected in 2027, while ARISTADA patents run to 2039 and LYBALVI patents to 2041, with LYBALVI facing paragraph IV challenges, and the legacy products rely on three wholesalers. LUMRYZ supplied 16.5% of nine-month 2026 revenue through four specialty pharmacies, bears a 3.85% royalty to Jazz and faces a generic challenge [business context: operating model and credit translations]. Cash from operations of USD 72.9 million for nine months 2026, against USD 350.7 million a year earlier, shows how heavily the first year of integration weighed on cash, while LTM free cash flow of USD 227.4 million shows the recovery to date [financial base: cash flow quality].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Documented behaviour is not extractive: no dividend has been paid and buybacks of USD 27.7 million occurred only in Q1 2026, but ownership, board and covenant capacity are not supplied, so legal capacity for distributions cannot be tested [business context: ownership, governance and capital allocation]. This corrects the business context handoff, which said buybacks stopped after the term loans were drawn: the sources show only that none occurred in Q2 or Q3 2026 and do not date the Q1 purchases against the February 12, 2026 closing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. (1) Liquidity and maturity profile: USD 787.6 million of cash and investments against light amortization and a 2031-weighted maturity wall, which gives time to absorb the 2027 VIVITROL change (Documentary Fact; financial base). (2) Cash generation: LTM free cash flow of USD 227.4 million with low capital spending, equal to 15.2% of debt (Documentary Fact for the inputs; the ratio is Analyst Interpretation). (3) Portfolio breadth beyond one product: four proprietary products plus royalties, with ARISTADA patents to 2039, LYBALVI to 2041 and LUMRYZ orphan exclusivity to 2030 for adults (Documentary Fact; business context). (4) Interest rate protection on USD 750.0 million of notional through collars entered in October 2026, though covenant effects are unknown (Documentary Fact). (5) Documented financial behaviour has been conservative: debt prepaid in 2024, no dividends, no buybacks in Q2 or Q3 2026 (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation on what it implies).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. (1) Dependence on add-backs: 3.40x on Adjusted EBITDA against 10.25x on reported EBITDA, with a derived FY2025 base and share-based compensation add-backs that do not tie to the statements (Documentary Fact; the dependence is Analyst Interpretation). (2) Product concentration and generic risk: VIVITROL at 31.7% of FY2025 revenue with generic entry expected in 2027, and product-level margins Not supplied, so the cash flow effect cannot be sized (Documentary Fact; Insufficient Information for the effect). (3) Secured structure without visible covenants: all debt is secured on substantially all assets, but levels, definitions and the margin grid are Not supplied, and Term Loan B is outside the maintenance tests (Insufficient Information). (4) Floating-rate exposure: Term SOFR plus 1.75% to 2.25% on Term Loan A and 2.25% on Term Loan B, half of principal hedged by collars (Documentary Fact; the share is arithmetic). (5) Acquisition accounting and contingent liability: a preliminary purchase price allocation, intangibles and goodwill that make up most of the consideration, and a possible payment of USD 165.7 million carried at USD 136.9 million (Documentary Fact; the impairment exposure is Analyst Interpretation). (6) Channel and counterparty concentration: three wholesalers for legacy products and four specialty pharmacies for LUMRYZ (Documentary Fact). (7) Thin interim cash conversion: nine-month 2026 cash from operations of USD 72.9 million (Documentary Fact).
